Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

questions.description: Questions to ask the user (1-4 questions)

question.description: The complete question to ask the user. Should be clear, specific, and end with a question mark. Example: "Which library should we use for date formatting?" If multiSelect is true, phrase it accordingly, e.g. "Which features do you want to enable?"

header.description: Very short label displayed as a chip/tag (max 12 chars). Examples: "Auth method", "Library", "Approach".

options.description: The available choices for this question. Must have 2-4 options. Each option should be a distinct, mutually exclusive choice (unless multiSelect is enabled). There should be no 'Other' option, that will be provided automatically.

label.description: The display text for this option that the user will see and select. Should be concise (1-5 words) and clearly describe the choice.

description.description: Explanation of what this option means or what will happen if chosen. Useful for providing context about trade-offs or implications.

preview.description: Optional preview content rendered when this option is focused. Use for mockups, code snippets, or visual comparisons that help users compare options. See the tool description for the expected content format.

multiSelect.description: Set to true to allow the user to select multiple options instead of just one. Use when choices are not mutually exclusive.

answers.description: User answers collected by the permission component

annotations.description: Optional per-question annotations from the user (e.g., notes on preview selections). Keyed by question text.

preview.description: The preview content of the selected option, if the question used previews.

notes.description: Free-text notes the user added to their selection.

metadata.description: Optional metadata for tracking and analytics purposes. Not displayed to user.

source.description: Optional identifier for the source of this question (e.g., "remember" for /remember command). Used for analytics tracking.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

This tool runs Git Bash (POSIX sh), not cmd.exe or PowerShell. Use Unix shell syntax: `/dev/null` not `NUL`, forward slashes, `$VAR` not `%VAR%` or `$env:VAR`. Do not use PowerShell here-strings (`@'…'@`) or backtick continuation here — for multi-line strings use a heredoc.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to modify

new_string.description: The text to replace it with (must be different from old_string)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences of old_string (default false)

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists agents you can SendMessage to — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access; a cloud session receives your message but cannot message any session back yet — do not ask it to reply, read its answer in its own transcript), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions — Remote Control sessions on other machines and cloud sessions, each row labeled by kind. Names are the address: send with `SendMessage({to: "<name>", message: "..."})`, copying the name exactly as a row prints it. Append a row's ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — two rows share it, or an error asks you to disambiguate.

channel.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

q.description: Not available in this build; leave unset.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes. With `run_in_background` the timeout is instead how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000ms / 30 minutes, max 7200000ms / 2 hours); at that limit it is stopped and you are notified.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 1800000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Write
tools.description:
Writes a file to the local filesystem, overwriting if one exists.

When to use: creating a new file, or fully replacing one you've already Read. Overwriting an existing file you haven't Read will fail. For partial changes, use Edit instead.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to write (must be absolute, not relative)

content.description: The content to write to the file

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__delegate_task
tools.description: Start one child agent with only `task`. No parent history. Separate checkout or PR per child: `isolation:'worktree'`. Keep `taskId` for `task_status` and `task_cancel`. No secrets in `task`.

options.description: Options from `orchestrator_capabilities`, such as {effort:'max'}. Given values override inherited. [] or {} clears.

isolation.description: 'shared' (default): parent checkout. 'worktree': new prepared checkout from the parent commit, for a separate checkout or PR per child. Uncommitted edits stay out.

mode.description: Default 'async'. 'wait' only if this turn needs the result. A question or approval ends the wait.

timeoutMs.description: Mode 'wait' only. At most 45 s. A timeout does not cancel the child.

runtimeMode.description: Omit unless the user asks for a supervised child. Narrow modes pause for human approval, not read-only. Above yours is rejected.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__link_pull_request
tools.description: Link a PR to this thread. T3 shows its status and settles the thread on merge. For several PRs, use `link_pull_requests`.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__orchestrator_capabilities
tools.description: List providers, models, options, and runtime modes for `delegate_task`. Short list. `search` finds others. Any catalog model works.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__request_secret
tools.description: Ask for one secret per single-line card; never combine values. Open it, don't offer it. Returns one-use `secretRef`, or `delivery: "file"` a file read only in its command, e.g. `adb pair <ip:port> "$(cat <file>)"`. Asked how: call now. Sign-in link: `url`. tools.name: mcp__t3-code__send_to_user
tools.description: Show the user a Markdown message in this thread, exactly as written, before your turn ends. Use it for content the user must read in full mid-turn, such as a draft, a code block, or what a question you are about to ask refers to. Don't repeat it in your reply.

tools.name: mcp__t3-code__t3_background_wait

input.title: #245 Edge instrumentation (resume)
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #245 in Moneo: instrumentation.ts touches `process.report` and other Node-only startup code, which gives an Edge-runtime warning at build time.

1. Run `npm run build` and check whether the warning still appears. If it doesn't, comment on the issue with the evidence (`gh issue comment 245`) and stop without opening a PR.
2. If it does, read the instrumentation guide in node_modules/next/dist/docs/. Move the Node-only work behind the supported boundary, for example a dynamic import of a Node-only module under `NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'`.
3. Keep the startup order: undici networking config, Workflow, scheduler, bank return listener. The desktop standalone build must still work.

## RESUME: earlier work may exist
A stopped agent may have left uncommitted work in `C:/Users/mgsuk/.t3/worktrees/Moneo/t3-ed0fca5a-64c8deb03b9c4d32` (branch `t3/issue-245-edge-instrumentation`).
- Inspect it read-only (`git -C <path> status`/`diff`) and bring over anything useful.
- Never modify, reset or delete that worktree.
- Use your own branch `t3/issue-245-edge-startup` from current `origin/main`.
- Commit as soon as the earlier work is applied.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 245 --comments`.
- End each commit message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait for installs and builds in the same turn: a foreground command with a long timeout, or a background command plus `t3_background_wait`. Finish the whole task before replying.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.** Never kill by name or command line.
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- Shared test backend:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`).
- Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build`. If 5-second timeouts under load show up in files you didn't touch, report them but don't change them.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #245`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

content.text:
#233 is up as [PR #253](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/253), and I'll merge it once CI is green. It does three things:
- The five modules that hold secrets now carry `import "server-only"`, so a build fails if one of them ends up in browser code.
- The `serviceDb` re-export in `lib/bank/server.ts` is gone, and every caller and test mock now imports it from `lib/service-db.ts`.
- AGENTS.md has a new rules row for this.

My main worry was that background jobs or startup code would crash on importing `server-only`, because loaded outside Next's usual rendering path it throws instead of doing nothing. I checked both sides:
- **Next:** it treats `server-only` as empty in all server code, which covers startup code.
- **Workflow builder:** it does the same when it bundles background jobs.
- **Elsewhere:** no script, desktop file or test outside Next imports these modules.

The agent couldn't run the desktop build on this machine. The PR changes `package.json`, so the Desktop CI workflow builds and smoke-tests all four platforms anyway.

I started the next agent in the queue, [#245 Edge instrumentation (resume)](t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A4ab48689-1401-4926-b4f6-fa0aa685ec23%3Adelegate-task%3A9e56244c-e6e8-4fce-86d3-cbc0d8952e38).

- **Running:** #235, #236, #232, #245.
- **Waiting for CI before merge:** [#250](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/250), [#252](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/252), [#253](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/253).
- **Still queued:** #237, #238, #188, #227 PR 1, #152.

Fix GitHub issue #237 in Moneo: make failures outside workflows observable, and enforce async handling.

1. Recount the empty catches and ignored promises in lib/, server actions and route handlers.
2. For each one, decide who owns the failure, then do one of three things: return an actionable failure, persist a job outcome, or route it to a named existing handler.
3. Add type-aware lint (no-floating-promises, no-misused-promises, switch-exhaustiveness-check) for lib/, workflows/ and server actions. Introduce it incrementally and keep lint time reasonable.
4. Don't add generic retries or catch-and-log wrappers, and never log financial data or credentials.
5. Add a row to the AGENTS.md rules table for the new enforcement.

If the full scope is too big for one reviewable PR, deliver the lint plus the fixes for lib/, and list the rest in the PR body.

- Never modify, reset or delete that worktree.

content.text:
#235 (time zones) is open as [PR #256](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/256). I've read the core of it and it looks right. I'll merge it once CI passes.

- **What changed:** functions that handle dates no longer quietly default to Europe/Berlin. The time zone is now a required argument, so code that leaves it out won't compile. The default comes from the device, and Settings offers "Use this device's timezone".
- **New rule:** lint now rejects a hard-coded `Europe/Berlin`, and AGENTS.md has a rules row for it.
- **Tests:** the suite passed under both UTC and Berlin, but only with a much longer test timeout, because the machine is heavily loaded.
- **Two places keep Berlin on purpose:**
  - Imports confirmed before Moneo saved a time zone with them still replay as Berlin, so their history doesn't change.
  - Berlin is also still the fallback in already-applied migrations and the database defaults. That's filed as #255.
- **Docker installs:** there, "device time zone" means the server's, which in a container is usually UTC. The owner's own device only sets it through the Settings button.
- **One failure locally:** `npm run test:db` failed with "fresh and upgraded schema differ". The PR adds no migration, so the shared test database likely still holds another branch's migration. CI builds a fresh database, so its database job is the real check.

Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting.

-New transactions are organized for you. Moneo first uses what your bank sent (merchant codes, counterparty, your own accounts for transfers and currency exchanges) and what you have already confirmed; the AI labels the rest. Labels the AI is sure about are applied right away and marked as AI; the ones it isn't sure about wait for you. **Money → AI organizer** lists both: answer a question once and every row from that payee follows, confirm or undo any AI decision, and edit what Moneo remembers. You can also ask about them in chat.

input.title: #188 import slowdown (resume)
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #188 in Moneo: import ingest slows down superlinearly. With `supabase/tests/import-batch-throughput.mjs` on moneo-qa, 10,000 rows take about 40 times as long as 1,000.

1. Measure first: run `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on `import_batch_candidates` and `ingest_import_batch` for the 1st batch and the 40th batch. Also check whether an `ANALYZE` after staging flattens the curve.
2. Find the real cause:
   - If it's in the SQL or a missing index, add a new ordered migration in supabase/migrations/ with a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160041`. Never rewrite an applied migration. Keep lib/schema.ts aligned. It must work on the desktop's bundled Postgres, so use no extensions it lacks.
   - If only the script's measurement is wrong, fix the script and explain why.
3. Make the throughput script assert a near-linear curve, so the slowdown can't come back.
4. Results must stay identical: the same transactions, dedup, history and undo.

The database is shared with other agents. Use rollback-only transactions and synthetic data, and note in the PR if concurrent load made the timings noisy.

input.title: #227 PR1 speech engines (resume)
input.task:
Moneo issue #227 (configurable speech-to-text for the CHAT MIC only; voice calls/GPT-Live untouched). You build **PR 1 of 4**: the engine contract, the Settings section and the fallback. No local model or OpenRouter yet; later PRs add those on top, so keep the contract clean.

Today the chat mic (lib/ai/use-voice-input.ts, lib/ai/voice-recorder.ts) streams PCM to OpenAI realtime transcription through app/api/voice/session/route.ts. That route uses gpt-live-transcribe with vocabulary hints from lib/ai/voice-vocabulary.ts, and the mic shows live words.

Build:
1. **Engine contract.** Create `lib/ai/speech/` with one engine contract: batch engines take the recorded audio plus hints and return text. The existing OpenAI live path becomes the `openai` engine, with unchanged behaviour. Add engine choice and fallback as a pure, unit-tested function:
   - If the chosen engine is unavailable or fails and an OpenAI key exists, use OpenAI and report that a fallback happened.
   - If there's no key, return a clear reason the mic can't work.
2. **Batch route.** A server route for batch engines (e.g. `app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts`). It accepts recorded audio (PCM16 or WAV, size-limited, validated with Zod) and calls the chosen engine, with owner auth like the other voice routes. Wire it to an engine registry. If it's small, add OpenAI batch transcription (/v1/audio/transcriptions) as a second mode; otherwise the registry alone is enough.
3. **Client.** Keep live streaming for `openai`. For batch engines, capture the audio and post it on Send/Done. Show a small note in the mic UI when the fallback was used. The Send/Done UX doesn't change.
4. **Settings.** Add a "Speech to text" section under Settings → Voice with the engine choice. Today only OpenAI is selectable; leave room for "On this computer" and "OpenRouter". Store it like the other owner preferences (see lib/settings.ts and its unreadable-preference test). Reset all data clears it.
5. **Tests.** Engine selection and fallback (fake engines), route validation and auth, audio encoding. No real API calls.

content.text:
#245 is fixed in [PR #258](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/258), and I'll merge it once CI is green.

- **Cause:** `instrumentation.ts` read `process.report` at the top of the file. The bundler saw that Node-only call even with the runtime check around it.
- **Fix:** the Node startup steps moved, unchanged, into `instrumentation-node.ts`. That file is only imported when the runtime is Node. The order stays the same: networking setup, Workflow, scheduler, bank return listener.
- **Build:** `npm run build` showed the Edge warning before the fix and doesn't after.
- **Desktop:** `npm run desktop:build` built the app, then stopped because the bundled backend isn't downloaded on this machine. So packaging and the smoke test weren't run. CI's desktop workflow won't cover it either, because this PR doesn't touch the files that trigger that workflow. The new file is imported by name, so the standalone build should include it, but nothing has actually started the desktop app with it.

- **Waiting for CI before merge:** #252, #253, #254, #257, #258.
- **Still queued:** #152.

content.content:
=== #158
Home is built for one currency (the workspace display currency) for now.

- Recorded net worth by currency: Home used to list each currency's recorded total and the observations behind it (removed with the redesign; the Wealth page still shows net worth per currency).
- Net worth chart: plots only display-currency balances and valuations; convert others with the rate dated on or before each month end.
- Cash flow (month card and six-month chart): no "partial" marker when rows lack a rate; surface it again once FX is handled.
- Budgets and Coming up: amounts in other currencies are left out.

_Moved from BACKLOG.md._

=== #161
Add German as an interface language, chosen in Settings.

A first pass was started in a worktree and discarded; this is what it did, as a starting point:

- `lib/settings.ts`: `locale` becomes `z.enum(["en-GB", "de-DE"])` (default `en-GB`) and doubles as the language preference.
- `app/settings/form.tsx`: replace the free-text "Date and number locale" field with a Language select (English / Deutsch) and update the help text ("The app is available in English only" goes away).
- `app/layout.tsx`: set `<html lang>` to `de` or `en` from the workspace locale.
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` and `app/api/artifacts/route.ts`: tell the model to answer and write artifacts in German when the locale is `de-DE`, keeping names and quoted user text as given.
- `app/settings/actions.test.ts`: test that saving `de-DE` persists the locale.

Still open:

- Translating the UI strings (pages, home widgets, command palette, errors). The first pass only switched the AI's language.
- Voice call language (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Existing workspaces whose stored locale is something other than `en-GB` / `de-DE` (the new enum would reject them).
- Mobile and light/dark check of the new select.


=== #255
Parent tracker: #224. Split out of #235.

Several applied migrations (reservation and reviewed-balance functions, wealth and goal date checks, budget rollover, bank observations, loan repayments) fall back to `'Europe/Berlin'` when a workspace has no `workspace_settings` row, and `workspace_settings.timezone` and `spending_plans.rollover_from` default to Berlin in the schema.

The app now saves the detected device time zone on the first workspace load (`requireWorkspace`), so the fallback is only reachable for a workspace that has not been loaded by the app yet.

Make the database follow the same rule: a new migration that replaces the functions so they raise when no zone is stored, and drops the column defaults, with `lib/schema.ts` aligned. It must run on the desktop backend (no extensions the bundle lacks) and must not rewrite applied migrations.

questions.question: #175 Chat memory (Moneo remembers what you teach it across chats, e.g. "Venji = Venjalin Ravindran", "my main card", "don't count rent in spending"): how should notes get saved?

options.label: Suggest a note card after a correction (Recommended)
options.description: When you correct Moneo, it offers "Remember that Venji is Venjalin?" as a card you tap. Saying "remember that…" also makes one. Notes are listed in Settings, editable and deletable, and loaded into chat and voice. They are never treated as financial truth.

options.label: Only when I say "remember"
options.description: Nothing gets proposed unless you ask.

options.label: Save automatically, no card
options.description: Least friction, but it's an AI write without your tap, which breaks the cards rule.

options.label: Not now
options.description: Leave it.

questions.question: #158 Multi-currency on Home (net worth chart, cash flow, budgets and Coming up ignore non-display currencies today): what should we do?

input.title: #152 Wealth charts and news
input.task:
Build Moneo issue #152: per-position price charts and news on the Wealth page for Scalable Capital positions.

The owner decided: **the chart comes from the last sync, and news loads live when the detail opens.**

**Detail view**
- Tapping a Scalable position on Wealth opens a detail view with a price chart. Use a drawer or page, whichever matches how the app shows transaction details.
- Offer the periods 1D/1W/1M/1Y/Max, as far as Scalable's `get_security_chart` timeframes allow.
- Mark the owner's own buys and sells on the chart from the stored trade history. lib/scalable/history.ts and history-job.ts already read charts and trade details, so reuse them.

**Storing the chart**
- Store the chart points during the regular Scalable sync (lib/scalable/sync.ts), so the chart works offline and opening it costs no extra calls.
- Add a new ordered migration with a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160041`. Keep lib/schema.ts aligned. It must work on the desktop's bundled Postgres.
- Prices are decimal text or integer minor units with an explicit currency, never floats for money. Use the formatter in lib/finance/format.ts.
- Show "as of <sync time>".

**News**
- Fetch it live from `get_security_news` when the detail opens, with a loading state and a clear offline/error state.
- Never block the chart on it.

**Scope and surfaces**
- Read-only: no trading changes.
- Check the mobile layout and both light and dark.
- If lib/scalable/read-tools.ts has an obvious spot, add a chat tool or artifact for "show me the chart for X".
- Disconnecting Scalable and "reset all data" must remove the stored chart data.
- Mock Scalable in tests. On the QA app, use a mocked or stand-in connection. Never call the real account.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 152 --comments`.
- Branch `t3/issue-152-wealth-charts` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step in plain language, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared with other agents:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`).
  - If 3100 is busy, wait and retry.
- If you apply your migration to the shared QA database for testing, revert it afterwards, so other branches' `test:db` isn't broken.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.**
- Also run `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:db`.
- Use the verify-ui skill for light/dark/mobile. Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #152`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

input.title: #152 Wealth charts and news
input.task:
Build Moneo issue #152: per-position price charts and news on the Wealth page for Scalable Capital positions.

The owner decided: **the chart comes from the last sync, and news loads live when the detail opens.**

**Detail view**
- Tapping a Scalable position on Wealth opens a detail view with a price chart. Use a drawer or page, whichever matches how the app shows transaction details.
- Offer the periods 1D/1W/1M/1Y/Max, as far as Scalable's `get_security_chart` timeframes allow.
- Mark the owner's own buys and sells on the chart from the stored trade history. lib/scalable/history.ts and history-job.ts already read charts and trade details, so reuse them.

**Storing the chart**
- Store the chart points during the regular Scalable sync (lib/scalable/sync.ts), so the chart works offline and opening it costs no extra calls.
- Add a new ordered migration with a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160041`. Keep lib/schema.ts aligned. It must work on the desktop's bundled Postgres.
- Prices are decimal text or integer minor units with an explicit currency, never floats for money. Use the formatter in lib/finance/format.ts.
- Show "as of <sync time>".

**News**
- Fetch it live from `get_security_news` when the detail opens, with a loading state and a clear offline/error state.
- Never block the chart on it.

**Scope and surfaces**
- Read-only: no trading changes.
- Check the mobile layout and both light and dark.
- If lib/scalable/read-tools.ts has an obvious spot, add a chat tool or artifact for "show me the chart for X".
- Disconnecting Scalable and "reset all data" must remove the stored chart data.
- Mock Scalable in tests. On the QA app, use a mocked or stand-in connection. Never call the real account.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 152 --comments`.
- Branch `t3/issue-152-wealth-charts` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step in plain language, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared with other agents:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend (.env, port 3000, project `moneo`).
  - If 3100 is busy, wait and retry.
- If you apply your migration to the shared QA database for testing, revert it afterwards, so other branches' `test:db` isn't broken.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.**
- Also run `npm test`, `npm run build` and `npm run test:db`.
- Use the verify-ui skill for light/dark/mobile. Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #152`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

input.title: #265 mac-arm64 quit leaves a process
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #265 in Moneo. In the desktop smoke test (`npm run desktop:smoke`, scripts/desktop/package-smoke.mjs), the check `quit stops every process` failed on mac-arm64 in the Desktop workflow for PR #253 (actions run 43915218876, job 133467406741, log `smoke-mac-arm64` artifact). It reported a leftover `Moneo#65851`. Windows and Linux passed. The server port was closed after quit.

1. Read the logs: `gh api repos/indkhan/Moneo/actions/jobs/133467406741/logs`, and download the `smoke-mac-arm64` artifact with `gh run download 43915218876 -n smoke-mac-arm64`.
2. Work out which process outlived quit. Moneo#<pid> is likely an Electron helper or a child the app spawned. Then work out why:
   - Look at the main process's quit/shutdown path in desktop/src (backend processes in desktop/src/backend/processes.ts and index.ts), and at how the smoke test samples processes.

input.title: #255 Berlin fallback in database
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #255 in Moneo: remove the Europe/Berlin fallback from database functions and column defaults. Read the issue for the list.

Several applied migrations fall back to `'Europe/Berlin'` when a workspace has no `workspace_settings` row:
- reservation and reviewed-balance functions
- wealth and goal date checks
- budget rollover
- bank observations
- loan repayments

`workspace_settings.timezone` and `spending_plans.rollover_from` also default to Berlin. Since PR #256, the app saves the detected device time zone on the first workspace load (`requireWorkspace`).

The work: add a new migration that replaces those functions so they raise a clear error when no zone is stored, and drops the column defaults. Keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned.
- Use a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160051`.
- Never rewrite an applied migration.
- It must run on the desktop backend, so use no extensions the bundle lacks.
- Re-create each function from its LATEST definition, changing only the fallback. Diff the old and new bodies to prove nothing else changed.
- Check that every path creating a workspace (setup, desktop bootstrap SQL in `desktop/bootstrap/`, the QA auth script, tests) still stores a time zone, so nothing starts raising.

#227 part 1 (the speech-to-text engine contract) is up as [PR #267](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/267). I'll merge it once CI is green.

- **What it adds:** one shared shape for speech engines, plus the rule for falling back to OpenAI. There's a new endpoint for engines that transcribe a finished recording; it checks the audio and caps it at 12 MB.
- **Settings:** a new Voice section holds "Speech to text" and the call voice picker, which moved there. Only OpenAI can be picked for now; "On this computer" and "OpenRouter" show as coming soon. The choice is saved in a new database column and cleared by "Reset all data".
- **Checks:** lint, typecheck, `npm test` and the build pass. Screenshots in light, dark and mobile are in the PR body.
- **Not checked by the agent:**
  - The full database migration replay hit a lock timeout twice on the shared test database. CI's database job covers it.
  - The real microphone path and the fallback note can't be tried here, because the test app has no real AI key. Only unit tests cover them.

I queued part 2 (local models, on Opus) to start once #267 is merged.

Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. Opening Moneo or coming back to it also syncs in the background (Scalable at most every 15 minutes, banks at most every hour): you see the last numbers right away and the page updates when the sync lands. If a value can't be refreshed, it still counts in your net worth and Wealth marks it as not from today. A short message in the corner of Home tells you once about old values and about a connection that failed or needs reconnecting.

-New transactions are organized for you. Moneo first uses what your bank sent (merchant codes, counterparty, your own accounts for transfers and currency exchanges) and what you have already confirmed; the AI labels the rest. Labels the AI is sure about are applied right away and marked as AI; the ones it isn't sure about wait for you. **Money → AI organizer** lists both: answer a question once and every row from that payee follows, confirm or undo any AI decision, and edit what Moneo remembers. You can also ask about them in chat.

I fixed #188 and opened PR #274. Each imported row's duplicate guard was reading every transaction in the workspace, so per-row work grew with history; after the fix a 10,000-row import costs about the same per row as a 1,000-row one. The old worktree had nothing uncommitted, so I started fresh from `origin/main`.

**Measurements.** `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` on every statement inside the two functions, for batch 1 and batch 40 of 10,000 rows:
- `import_batch_candidates` is flat, at about 2,000 blocks per batch.
- `ingest_import_batch` grows from about 30k blocks in batch 1 to about 2.5M in batch 40. Of that, 2.48M is one statement in `ingest_import_row_internal`: the "Import candidates changed" guard.
- Running `ANALYZE` after staging doesn't flatten the curve on the old code (383 s of ingest, still growing).

**Cause and fix.** The guard put the duplicate match (date, amount, description) and an external-ID lookup in one OR, so the database couldn't use the indexes on `description` or `external_id`. New migration `202611160081_import_guard_index_paths.sql` splits it into two separate checks with the same conditions, each using its index. It's the split `import_batch_candidates` already uses. No new index, and no extensions the desktop's bundled Postgres lacks. I numbered it after 0051 and 0061, which other branches have already applied on the QA database. `lib/schema.ts` doesn't change.

**Throughput script.** It also had a measurement problem. All 10,000 rows were on one day, in tables that are never analyzed, so even after the fix the guard scanned the whole day for each row. It now spreads the rows over a year; the old code still explodes with spread dates, so the migration is the real fix. The script now asserts on buffer blocks per row, because wall times on the loaded database varied up to 5×:

| | 1,000 rows | 10,000 rows | result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `main` | 147 | 6,018 | fails (41×) |
| this PR | 147 | 280 | passes (bound is 3×) |

What's left of the growth is `recount_import_progress`, which recounts the whole import after every batch for the live progress display. I filed that as #272.

**Results unchanged.** The script's exact counts, totals and source-row checks pass. I added checks to `supabase/tests/import-batches.sql` proving both halves of the split guard still block a duplicate. They fail if I disable the external-ID half.

**Checks:**
- `npm run lint`: last line `> eslint .`, no errors.
- `npm run typecheck`: last line `> tsc --noEmit && tsc --noEmit -p desktop`, no errors.
- `npm test`: 303 files and 1,719 tests passed, with no 5-second timeouts.
- `npm run test:db` fails, but not because of this change; the cause is the shared QA database.
  - The fresh replay of 136 migrations and 60 SQL tests passes, including the new checks.
  - The upgrade replay fails in `atomic-review.sql` because another branch's `202611160061_workspace_time_zone_required` is applied there.
  - In the live tests, 8 files pass, including both import tests. `schema.live`, `evidence-receipts.live` and `review-request.live` fail on that same other-branch schema.

Other worktrees recreated the QA database three times while I worked, so timings were noisy. The PR says so. My test runs were all rollback-only, and the QA migration history is unchanged.

PR https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/274, head b4159fcd699f76b64fa60be78b8dfaadc2cd746b, checks and reviews: GitGuardian passed; checks, database, browser and desktop builds in progress; no review yet.

input.title: #261 IBAN normalization bug
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #261 in Moneo. `ownAccountIbans` in `workflows/bank-sync.ts` normalizes IBANs with `.replace(/s/g, "")` instead of `/\s/g`, so it strips the letter "s" instead of spaces.

1. Reproduce it with a failing unit test. Extend `workflows/bank-sync.test.ts`, or better, test the normalization through the existing shared helper.
2. Look for an existing `normalizeIban` in lib/ (lib/finance/own-transfers.ts imports one). Use that helper instead of a second inline regex, so this class of bug can't come back. Fix the cause, not just the character.
3. Search for other inline IBAN normalizations (`git grep -n "replace(/s\|replace(/\\\\s" -- lib workflows app`) and route them through the same helper if any exist.

- **Cause:** each imported row ran a duplicate check that read every transaction in the workspace, so imports got slower as history grew. The check put two lookups into one query, and the database couldn't use its indexes for either.
- **Fix:** a new migration splits the check into two queries with the same conditions, each using its own index. It adds no index and needs no extensions, so it also runs on the desktop app's database.
- **Results unchanged:** new SQL tests show both halves still block a duplicate. They fail if one half is turned off.
- **The throughput script was also misleading:** it put all 10,000 rows on one day. It now spreads them over a year and checks database blocks read per row instead of time, because timings on the shared database varied up to 5×.
- **Remaining slowdown:** the import's progress counter recounts the whole import after every batch. That's filed as #272.
- **Local `npm run test:db` failed:** other branches' migrations were applied to the shared test database. The fresh replay with the new checks passed. CI uses a clean database.

Next from the queue: [#261 IBAN normalization bug](t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A4ab48689-1401-4926-b4f6-fa0aa685ec23%3Adelegate-task%3A08e958cf-ec8b-4e46-a2c4-766e015fa0c3), on Haiku. I told it to use the shared `normalizeIban` helper rather than fix only the regex.

- **Running:** #152, #265, #255, #261.
- **Waiting for checks before merge:** #253, #258, #266, #274.
- **Still queued:** #262, #263, #264, then #227 part 2.

Delegated task node:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A4ab48689-1401-4926-b4f6-fa0aa685ec23%3Adelegate-task%3A1b9ecc24-60b8-4a66-8ea3-a1ea4796e6a1 (#255 Berlin fallback in database) [completed]:
PR #275 is open for #255 and not merged. Lint, typecheck and `npm test` pass, but `npm run test:db` fails in its upgrade half because of other branches' migrations in the shared QA database.

**What changed**
- **Migration:** `202611160061_workspace_time_zone_required.sql` adds `workspace_time_zone(workspace_id)`, which raises `Workspace time zone is not set` (SQLSTATE 55000) when no zone is stored.
- **Functions:** It rewrites the ten functions that fell back to Berlin to call it. They are patched from their live definitions, not copied from the old files. A later migration (`202610310001`) rewrote `40001` to `PT409` inside them, and copying the old text would have undone that.
- **Diff check:** I dumped the ten functions before and after on the QA database. Only the Berlin fallback lines differ. The migration also fails if any `Europe/Berlin` is left in a function.
- **Defaults:** It drops the defaults on `workspace_settings.timezone` and `spending_plans.rollover_from`, and `lib/schema.ts` matches.
- **`rollover_from`:** A before-insert trigger now fills `rollover_from` from the workspace zone. That keeps the two app code paths that insert spending plans unchanged.
- **Workspace creation paths:** None of them stores a zone, so nothing there needed changes. Setup, desktop bootstrap and the QA auth script leave it to the first workspace load (`requireWorkspace`).
- **Tests and scripts:** About 20 SQL fixtures, `.mjs` tests, live tests and `voice-call-check.mjs` now insert a zone before calling these functions. In the two fixtures that seed every table generically, `reset-workspace.sql` and `workspace-isolation.sql`, I moved `workspace_settings` first in the table list and gave it a zone.

**Last lines of each check**
- `npm run lint`: clean, no output (exit 0).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean, no output (exit 0).
- `npm test`: `Test Files 304 passed | 11 skipped (315)`, `Tests 1725 passed | 17 skipped (1742)`.
- `npm run test:db`: the first half passes: `PASS: fresh replay 137 migrations and 61 SQL regressions; disposable schema rollback verified`. The upgrade half then fails with `Upgrade SQL regression reset-workspace.sql: Missing reset fixture for table scalable_security_charts; update reset coverage`. The shared QA database now has other branches' migrations applied (e.g. `202611160137`), so the failure is not from this change. It was not a lock timeout, so I did not retry.
- The live vitest suites pass except `lib/schema.live.test.ts`, which fails for the same reason: its diff lists only other branches' tables and columns (`scalable_security_charts`, `speech_engine`).
- `reservation-balance-concurrency.mjs` passes.

**QA database:** I applied the migration to `moneo-qa` while testing, then reverted it. The ten function definitions match the dump taken before, the defaults are back and the migration row is gone. The QA database container also restarted once during my runs. I did not touch it and it came back healthy.

input.title: #262 Regenerate replaces reply
input.task:
Fix GitHub issue #262 in Moneo. Since PR #250, Regenerate (components/message-actions.tsx, the RESEND_EVENT listener in components/chat-form.tsx) resends the last question. That appends a duplicate question and a second answer. Change it so that:

- Regenerate replaces the last assistant reply with a new one and does not duplicate the user's question.
- The earlier answer stays reachable, e.g. a small "1/2 ‹ ›" switcher or "previous answers" under the reply, like ChatGPT.
- It survives reload. Check how messages and chat_requests are stored (lib/ai/conversation-history.ts, app/api/chat/route.ts) and pick the smallest correct storage change, for example marking a reply as a regeneration of an earlier request. Never delete history; AGENTS.md says history is kept.
- If you add a migration, give it a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160141`, keep lib/schema.ts aligned, and make sure it works on the desktop's Postgres.
- Voice calls and artifacts are unaffected. Check that queued messages and steering still behave.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 262`.
- Branch `t3/issue-262-regenerate-replace` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait for it in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend.
  - If you apply a migration to QA, revert it afterwards.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.** Also run `npm test` and `npm run build`.
- Use the verify-ui skill (light/dark/mobile). Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #262`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

Fix GitHub issue #262 in Moneo. Since PR #250, Regenerate (components/message-actions.tsx, the RESEND_EVENT listener in components/chat-form.tsx) resends the last question. That appends a duplicate question and a second answer. Change it so that:

- Regenerate replaces the last assistant reply with a new one and does not duplicate the user's question.
- The earlier answer stays reachable, e.g. a small "1/2 ‹ ›" switcher or "previous answers" under the reply, like ChatGPT.
- It survives reload. Check how messages and chat_requests are stored (lib/ai/conversation-history.ts, app/api/chat/route.ts) and pick the smallest correct storage change, for example marking a reply as a regeneration of an earlier request. Never delete history; AGENTS.md says history is kept.
- If you add a migration, give it a unique timestamp prefix later than `202611160141`, keep lib/schema.ts aligned, and make sure it works on the desktop's Postgres.
- Voice calls and artifacts are unaffected. Check that queued messages and steering still behave.

## Rules
- Read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly. Read `gh issue view 262`.
- Branch `t3/issue-262-regenerate-replace` from current `origin/main`. Commit each step, ending each message with:
  Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Don't end your turn while a command is still running.** Wait for it in the same turn.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start yourself in this session, verified by PID.**
- Run one `npm ci` at a time. If it stalls, retry once with `--prefer-offline`.
- The QA app on port 3100 and the moneo-qa backend are shared:
  - Never run `npm run qa:reset` or `docker compose -p moneo-qa down`.
  - Never touch the owner's backend.
  - If you apply a migration to QA, revert it afterwards.
- **Run `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` yourself and quote their last lines in your final reply.** Also run `npm test` and `npm run build`.
- Use the verify-ui skill (light/dark/mobile). Link the screenshots in the PR body from a commit, then remove them from the branch.
- Push and open a PR to `main` (`Closes #262`), ending the body with:
  🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
  Never merge.
- Final line: PR <full URL>, head <SHA>, checks and reviews <state>.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing the dynamic patching approach, which is clever but risky since it changes whatever function definitions exist at run time. 274 probably also rewrites ingest_import_row_internal through its live definition, so I need to check whether that function contains Europe/Berlin. If it does, 275 patches it first and then 274's regex step picks up the updated definition, which works because 274 is dynamic too.

Since the earlier stretch already settled the order question, I'm now looking at the edge case: a workspace with no settings row would make these functions raise. I'm checking whether background jobs like bank sync could hit that before the first load after the upgrade, though existing workspaces should already have rows from the original Berlin default.

content.text:
I've reviewed #255's database fix ([PR #275](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/275)) and I'm waiting for CI before merging. Meanwhile the next queued agent, [#262 Regenerate replaces reply](t3-thread://v2/88042f69-c439-49f6-a4b9-1fb5180f2502/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3A4ab48689-1401-4926-b4f6-fa0aa685ec23%3Adelegate-task%3Ac7765292-4575-490b-8777-34f7de5f5abc), has started.

- **What #275 does:** ten database functions no longer fall back to Europe/Berlin when a workspace has no time zone saved. They now stop with a clear "Workspace time zone is not set" error. The two Berlin column defaults are gone too. A small trigger fills in the spending-plan rollover date from the workspace's own zone.
- **How the migration works:** it doesn't paste in old copies of those functions. It edits the live definitions in place and refuses to finish if any Europe/Berlin is left. Copying the old text would have undone a later fix to the same functions.
- **Fit with #274:** both PRs edit database functions this way, so the order they merge in doesn't matter. I also checked that the app applies any migration not yet applied, regardless of file order.
- **Existing installs:** a workspace without a saved time zone will now get an error instead of Berlin. Existing workspaces already have a saved zone, and new ones get it saved the first time the app opens them.
- **Local `npm run test:db` failed:** the shared test database has other branches' migrations applied. CI's database job starts from a clean one, so it's the real check.

- **Running:** #152, #265, #261, #262.
- **Waiting for checks before merge:** #253, #258, #274, #275.
- **Still queued:** #263, #264, then #227 part 2.

content.text:
#261 (the IBAN fix) is up as [PR #276](https://github.com/indkhan/Moneo/pull/276), and I'm changing one part of it before merging.

The agent moved every IBAN cleanup into one shared helper, `normalizeIban`, which is good. But that helper returns nothing for any value that isn't a valid IBAN. In three places that store what the bank sends, an account identifier that isn't an IBAN, such as a UK account number, would have been saved as empty. AGENTS.md says to keep source records as they arrive, so that's data loss.

My change adds `compactIban`, which strips spaces and uppercases without validating. Those three storage spots now use it, so they keep the bank's value. Matching your own accounts still uses the strict version, as before. The fix for the original bug, where the letter "s" was stripped instead of spaces, stays in.

Typecheck, lint and the bank tests are running locally. I'll push once they pass.
